title: A teenager and his dog found Lascaux’s Ice Age paintings in 1940
body: On 12 September 1940, 18-year-old Marcel Ravidat followed his dog to a hole left by an uprooted tree near Montignac, France, and came back with three friends to explore. Inside were more than 600 wall paintings of animals such as horses, deer and aurochs, usually dated to about 17,000–22,000 years ago. Visitors’ breath, heat and humidity soon damaged them, so the cave closed in 1963, and the public now visits replicas.

slides.question: Of every 10 animals painted at Lascaux, how many are horses?
slides.explanation: About 6 in 10: of the 605 animal figures identified precisely, 364 are equines. Stags come next, with 90.

slides.question: Why did Lascaux close to the public in 1963?
options: The roof was about to collapse
The paintings were moved to a museum
slides.explanation: Breath, heat and humidity from visitors soon damaged the paintings, so the cave closed and the public now visits replicas.
